attributes.description: Fires when a filesystem on the project node is running out of space. The data volume filling up stops database writes; the root volume filling up breaks the platform. WAL accumulation and pinned replication slots are the usual non-obvious causes.
attributes.name: [Supabase OTel] Filesystem nearly full

investigation_guide.blob:
## Filesystem Nearly Full

Running out of disk is terminal for writes and is one of the few Supabase failure modes with no graceful degradation. Mountpoints are not equivalent — read the `attributes.mountpoint` value on the alert before deciding urgency.

### Triage Steps
1. Identify what is consuming the space. Check database size per database (`pg_database_size_bytes` by `attributes.datname`) and WAL size (`pg_wal_size_mb`).
2. Check for a pinned replication slot. An inactive slot retains WAL indefinitely and will fill the volume regardless of how much data the tables hold: `TS metrics-supabase.metrics.otel-* | STATS slot_lag = MAX(LAST_OVER_TIME(replication_slots_max_lag_bytes)) BY resource.attributes.supabase_project_ref`
3. Check the WAL archive backlog (`pg_ls_archive_statusdir_wal_pending_count`). Segments that cannot be archived are not recycled.
4. Check temp file spill (`pg_stat_database_temp_bytes_total`), which indicates queries exceeding `work_mem` and writing to disk.
5. Watch for the filesystem flipping read-only, which is the next stage of this failure and has its own rule.

### Tuning
The rule uses `node_filesystem_avail_bytes` rather than `free_bytes` because available space excludes the root-reserved blocks that PostgreSQL cannot use. Tighten the 85% threshold on small volumes where 15% headroom is only a few hundred megabytes, and uncomment the `fstype` filter if your collector reports ephemeral mounts.
